user.title: Connect an Orgaia group
user.description:
In the Orgaia app, open **Group › Home Assistant** and tap "Open in Home Assistant". The link is copied by then: paste it here. An admin of the group then confirms Home Assistant in the app.

Everything stays end-to-end encrypted: Home Assistant gets its own key and reads the group like a member. It is not counted as a person.

data_description.link: The link from the app, starting with https://…/join# or orgaia://join?

reauth_confirm.title: Connect {group} again
reauth_confirm.description: Home Assistant is no longer a member of {group}. Create a new link for Home Assistant in the app and paste it here.

reconfigure.title: Connect {group} again
reconfigure.description: Joins {group} again with a new link and a new key. Entities and automations stay; the old key leaves the group. Create a new link for Home Assistant in the app and paste it here.

ready.title: {group} is connected
ready.description:
One more look, and the day is on the wall.

**Who is who?** People with the same name are matched already. That way Home Assistant knows who ticks something off on their own phone, and notifications reach the right person.

**Dashboard:** today, the shopping and the week as a ready-made page in the sidebar. If you would rather build your own, put the Orgaia card on a dashboard of yours.

progress.wait_for_admin:
Almost done. Open the Orgaia app: there **{group}** asks whether Home Assistant may connect.

Does the app show the same as here?

# {code}

If so, confirm there. This window waits for up to 10 minutes.

create_entry.default:
**{group}** is connected. The group's dashboard is in the sidebar now (if chosen), and the **Orgaia card** can be put on any dashboard.

Home Assistant only reads the group. An admin allows ticking off and adding in the Orgaia app under **Group › Home Assistant**.

needs_plus.title: Orgaia Plus ended for {group}
needs_plus.description: Home Assistant can read **{group}** only while the group has Orgaia Plus. Renew Plus in the app; Home Assistant picks up again by itself.

update_required.title: Update the Orgaia integration
update_required.description: The Orgaia server no longer accepts this version of the integration, so **{group}** is not updated. Install the latest version in HACS and restart Home Assistant.

write_not_allowed.title: {group}: Home Assistant may not tick off yet
write_not_allowed.description: Something was to be ticked off or added from Home Assistant, but no admin of {group} allowed that yet. In the Orgaia app, open Group › Home Assistant and switch on "May tick off and add". This notice goes away by itself once it is allowed.

dashboard_missing.title: {group}: the Orgaia dashboard is missing
dashboard_missing.description: The ready-made dashboard of **{group}** could not be put into the sidebar, most likely because this version of Home Assistant changed how dashboards work inside. Nothing else is affected: the Orgaia card and all entities go on working. Build a dashboard of your own with the Orgaia card, or switch off "Show the Orgaia dashboard in the sidebar" under Configure; then this hint goes away. An update of the integration usually brings the dashboard back.

persons.title: People of the group
persons.description: Choose which Home Assistant person each person of the group is. Events and person sensors then also name the person entity, e.g. for notifications, and that user may tick off and add in the standard to-do cards. People with the same name are suggested.
